title: A short history of the web

props.title: A short history of the web
props.subtitle: From one proposal to billions of pockets

scenes.shows: A timeline axis from 1989 to 2016 draws itself. The 1989 and 1993 milestones appear in turn, and each glows while its caption is on screen.

props.title: The beginnings
captions: 1989: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the web at CERN, to share research.
1993: the Mosaic browser shows images next to text, and people notice.

scenes.shows: The same timeline, with the earlier milestones dimmed. 1998 and 2004 appear in turn.

props.title: Finding and sharing
captions: 1998: Google is founded, and finding things gets much easier.
2004: the idea of "Web 2.0" spreads, as readers become writers too.

scenes.shows: The same timeline. 2007 and 2016 appear, and then the whole line lights up.

props.title: In every pocket
captions: 2007: the iPhone puts the full web in a pocket.
2016: worldwide, phones and tablets overtake computers for browsing.

scenes.shows: How different the web was in 1993

props.title: Still under construction
takeaways: The web began as a way to share research
Each new step let more people take part
